html:
Caucasian Albania was an ancient kingdom in the eastern Caucasus, roughly modern Azerbaijan and southern Dagestan. It has nothing to do with Albania in the Balkans; the Greeks and Romans used the name. It is shown here in 700.

It existed from around the 2nd century BCE and sat between Rome, Parthia, Armenia and later the Sasanian Empire, whose vassal it usually was. Its capital moved from Kabalaka to Partav, now Barda. In the early 4th century, soon after Armenia adopted Christianity, its king followed. According to tradition, Mesrop Mashtots, who made the Armenian alphabet, also made an alphabet for its language, and texts in that script have been found at Mount Sinai.

In the 7th century the Mihranid prince Javanshir balanced between the Byzantines, the Khazars and the Arabs. The Umayyad Arabs then took over, and around 705 they ended the local dynasty. Under Arab rule the region was called Arran.
